The research activity will focus on microbial populations associated with food and agro-environmental matrices using culture-dependent and -independent approaches. Main microbial groups will be quantified using conventional microbiological techniques and selective and/or differential media. Microorganisms of interest will be isolated, purified, identified, and preserved for phenotypic and functional characterization. DNA extracted directly from the matrices will be used for metataxonomic analyses targeting the 16S rRNA and ITS/26S rRNA genes. The research programme aims to investigate and valorise the genetic and functional diversity of alpha-amylase/trypsin inhibitors (ATIs) in wheat to develop healthier and more sustainable varieties and food products. The activities will include the genomic characterisation of a broad panel of *Triticum* genotypes through targeted long-read sequencing, analysis of variation at ATI loci, and integration of genomic data with information on ATI content and immunostimulatory potential.
